result.topic_en: A two-column Kant-style list of antinomies (thesis vs. antithesis): finitude vs. infinity and continuity, freedom vs. determinism, a God acting in time vs. a timeless God, and immortality vs. a thing-in-itself, with a note on reconciling freedom with natural law.

items.english: So that, despite completely determined laws of the action of representations, decisions by free will are possible, one must assume that the mental mechanism itself has (a sudden change?), the capacity, or at least attains in its development the capacity, to bring about the necessity of these decisions.

items.english: Freedom is quite compatible with the lawfulness of the course of nature. But alongside it, the concept of a timeless God is not tenable.

items.english: The concept of providence must be supplemented by the concept of world-governance.
